residualRegister.fix: H1: adding retrieve_result breaks exact built-in-surface assertions in cmd/mcp-bridge (serve_hybrid_exposure_test.go:201; serve_hybrid_reload_test.go:225,238,262; serve_hybrid_progressive_reveal_lifecycle_test.go:278-286,492; serve_hybrid_progressive_reveal_test.go:352-390; serve_oauth_test.go:449,500) that are neither write roots nor owned by a task; enumerate the complete assertion set from a directory-wide search and own it.

H2: session-less retrieval is admitted to the publisher projection by admitExposureRequest (session_exposure.go:105-120), so the observable is invalid_handle in that namespace, not rejection; AC17 as written cannot pass.
H3: the changed-claim list omits README.md:288, :338 and :443, so T6 greps pass while documented claims stay false.
H4: R1/R3 assert absolute 1536/8192 while §4.5 makes both ceilings configurable; state that the preview and page bounds are the configured ceilings.
H5: oracles for AC1,2,3,4,5,7,8,9,10,11,14 appear in no task -run; AC2 is owned by T1, which may not wire handlers.
H6: zero content is false; errorResult always emits one TextContent, so require zero retained-result or page bytes and assert that.
L1: remaining_pages/remaining_bytes arithmetic is undefined, so any convention passes.
L2: preview/page shapes cannot appear in a stored input schema and AC6 does not test that clause.
L3: handle_ttl is omitted from config validation, so zero or negative is accepted and expires every handle immediately.
L4: T7 validation writes coverage.out while T7 prohibits any write and no write root covers it.

R1: the claimed-complete built-in inventory misses internal/service/tool_metadata_test.go:108-120, internal/service/tools_publish_atomic_test.go:50-57 and cmd/mcp-bridge/serve_test.go:618, so T3 fails inside its envelope; make the inventory repo-complete and every hit a write root.

R2: unbounded upstream_code is copied into the preview and every page while the partition assumes bounded metadata, so a long code breaks the 1536 preview or the 8192 page with no truncation or termination rule.

R3: R7/AC15 require rejecting an out-of-range page before store access, but total_pages needs the owner-namespaced lookup, and page is optional with default 1; split pre-store shape checks from post-lookup range checks.
R4: the four metrics need internal/observe/metrics.go and the new events need docs/logging-contract.md, neither of which is a write root or expected file, while §8 ties metric scraping to AC9/T2.
R5: R6 requires preview/page shapes in the tool description, but AC6 checks only the stored input schema and README and no task owns description text.

R6: the unretainable branch specifies no Content prefix and never states that MCP isError mirrors the original, so AC13 passes with a metadata-only preview and an unretainable error can ship with isError false.

R7: the invalidation list omits SDK-session-loss retirement (inbound.go:800-816 retires the owner; :850/:921 mint a new epoch) while T2 names only reaper purge, so unreachable old-incarnation entries hold the aggregate cap.
R8: T6 negative greps forbid phrases that §6 requires documenting as still true at or below the ceiling, so T6 blocks truthful qualified wording.

M1: config validation bounds only max_metadata_envelope_bytes < delivery_ceiling_bytes, so a loadable config can make the preview non-empty-content requirement impossible (preview ceiling below preview metadata, whose digit widths are derived from a bound that cannot bound an unretained total_bytes); add a preview-feasibility validation and typed fallback.

M2: R10/§4.6 promise the full upstream code byte-exact on every branch while §4.2 truncates it, and the unretainable branch has no retained result; scope the promise to the retainable branch and state the unretainable observable.
L1: the description half names no observable, so a description with no paging fields passes; name the tokens the description must carry.

L2: rehydration never retires an epoch-bearing owner (newLiveOwner runs only when the record epoch is 0 at inbound.go:609/850/921), so the four-seam purge claim is vacuous; state epoch-keyed namespaces plus purge on reaper, DELETE and SDK-session-loss, and state both observables when a caller presents a retired epoch.
L3: the four collectors and new log events are tied to AC9/AC10 but no R/AC verifies them, so their deliverables can neither pass nor fail; add an AC or mark them advisory.

F1: feasibility constants bound structured metadata only, omitting the content-block wrapper, isError and a worst-case first-content-byte reserve, so a validated config can still yield an empty prefix; bound the complete serialized preview or page minus content plus a single-byte worst-case reserve.

F2: pages are sized against a configured ceiling that a supported reload may change while handles survive, shifting page boundaries or exceeding the new ceiling; pin the ceiling at retention or invalidate handles on change.
F3: AC8 assigns caller-visible expired/evicted results and their log events to T2, whose scope forbids handler wiring, while T3 owns the handler without AC8; reassign those assertions to T3.
F4: go test -coverprofile does not run the repository 90% gate (go run ./cmd/covcheck) and omits -coverpkg/-covermode used by .github/workflows/verify.yml; name the actual gate command.

F5: the periodic TTL sweep has no oracle or lifecycle owner in T2 write roots, and a per-request sweep cannot reclaim a live idle session; assign lifecycle plus an entries-gauge observable or mark it advisory.

F6: 8 MiB equals the transport default rather than headroom, and the claim that too_large is unreachable under defaults is false because the measured form duplicates content and structured forms plus escaping; derive the bound or document preview-only for oversize.
F7: the retainable-branch truncation marker has no oracle; AC10 asserts only the byte-exact code and AC16 covers the unretainable branch.
F8: the README claim that executions return the upstream result unaltered becomes false over-ceiling but is absent from the changed-claims list and T6 negative greps.
F9: upstream_code is specified as string-or-null and also as otherwise omitted; state one serialized form matched by the byte fixture.

H1: max_bytes_per_session (8 MiB) is hard while max_retained_result_bytes is derived from the transport cap inflated by duplicated forms and escaping, so a reachable result exceeds the hard bound and no terminal outcome exists; require per-session bytes >= the maximal single retained entry and state it.
M1: AC13 names one oracle owned by both T4 and T5 (duplicate symbol or unowned half) and T4 cannot pass before T5 exists; give unique per-task oracle names and state which surfaces each covers.

M2: collectors are claimed registered in the ops registry but observe.Metrics reaches the surface only through cmd/mcp-bridge/serve.go:164, outside every write root, and §8 contradicts itself on private registries; also four versus five collectors. Name the injection path and count.

M3: all session-less callers resolve to one publisherOwner, so cross-caller eviction isolation is false for that namespace and AC9 cannot distinguish; state namespace granularity and mutual evictability.

M4: T6 checks are jointly unsatisfiable — a positive grep for result_too_large, which the spec removes, plus negative greps forbidding strings §6 keeps in qualified form; make the check set consistent.
M5: the seam-after-commitDiscovery instruction has no behavioral oracle; require that after an over-ceiling search_tools the owner still sees the matched tools in tools/list.
L1: the only-terminal-case claim is false — entropy failure and envelope infeasibility are fail-closed internal_error outcomes with no handle; AC13 must say no handle-less preview.
L2: no AC asserts the preview text block carries a non-empty UTF-8-safe prefix, so a metadata-only preview passes.
L3: tombstone overflow loses the expired/evicted classification before tombstone_ttl, so determinism is overstated; qualify and add the overflow oracle.

H1: maximal_entry_bytes names escape_reserve and fixed_envelope without quantifying either; with a correct reserve the derived entry exceeds max_bytes_aggregate, and with an undercount the entry exceeds the hard per-namespace bound with no defined outcome. State computable derivations and the outcome when one entry cannot fit.

M1: the soft aggregate cap is untied to namespace count, so worst-case retained bytes is namespaces times per-namespace bound, far above the documented 64 MiB; state maximum exposure and either a hard total with an outcome or an advisory-only statement.
M2: T6 never falsifies the three changed completion claims, and a single positive grep can pass while README still claims the unqualified completeness; assert per claim.
L1: no oracle covers a reused session ID with a new epoch, and monotonic non-reuse of (sessionID, epoch) is assumed rather than stated.
L2: T2 owns TestTombstoneOverflow for AC8 but its AC-ID list omits AC8.
L3: upstream_code is defined only for a string code and the 128-byte bound has no rune-safety rule, so numeric or absent codes and multibyte truncation are unassertable.

F1: the per-entry bound assumes one copy and no escaping, but call_tool emits the upstream content twice and re-marshaling can escape 6x, and the upstream response cap is read from config yet never enforced on reads; define one entry metric, derive the maximum from duplicated forms plus escaping under an enforced cap, and require the hard bound to admit it or add a typed capacity terminal.

F2: R1 is unscoped while pages use the pinned ceiling, so a lowered ceiling makes a pinned page exceed the configured one and R1 demands re-paging, contradicting R4; state that retrieval pages are exempt from the current ceiling and bounded by the pinned one.
F3: two of R1 three terminal branches have no inducible oracle; name injectable entropy and a store-construction failure oracle in T2, or narrow R1/AC13.
F4: crypto-random is not falsified by a distinctness check a counter passes; name the entropy source oracle or mark unpredictability inspection-only.
F5: the spec changes the owner-adopted retention bound without a recorded amendment; the coordinator has now recorded a technical amendment in decisions.md, and the spec must cite it.
H1: the enforced cap needs Command.MaxResponseBytes in NewClient via cmd/mcp-bridge/wiring.go:159 and internal/upstream/runtime.go:154, neither of which is a write root or T2 expected file.

H2: a cap installed on the shared HTTPClient bounds every upstream body including discovery lists and the long-lived SSE GET, whose supported volumes exceed 8 MiB, so valid catalogs fail and streams die.
M1: an over-cap body yields a dispatch error before the seam, contradicting the universal preview+handle claim.
M2: C_envelope=256 undercounts the bridge envelope (server, wire tool name, request id, wrapper keys), so a maximal entry can exceed the hard bound.
M3: TestEnvelopeInfeasibility has no inducible seam and the config-load validation makes the terminal unreachable.
M4: pairwise distinctness passes for a counter or a content-derived handle, so unguessability has no oracle.
L1: decisions.md records 16 MiB while the spec uses 100663552 bytes and a 384 GiB worst-case exposure; the change is unrecorded.
OQ: call_tool has no owner-rejection path and inbound stamps no epoch when sessionEpoch is zero; epoch-0 sessions may be rejected by a rule the spec assumes exists.
F-01: a stale "(escape-dense-aware, open question)" marker contradicts settled auto-decision 3 and the TestEscapeDensePageFill oracle.
L1: a stale "(escape-dense-aware, open question)" marker contradicts settled auto-decision 3 and the TestEscapeDensePageFill oracle.
L2: wording clarity item reported as advisory; no invariant change.

F1: call_tool on a minted session with a present-but-invalid epoch header has no defined namespace; requiresExposure skips epoch validation for call_tool and requestExposureEpoch collapses absent and invalid headers, so a publisher fallback would expose the result to other session-less callers.
A1: "exactly the pinned headroom" is not realisable; a single re-escaped byte consumes one of six headroom bytes. Drop "exactly" or construct a multi-backslash fixture.
A2: invalid_handle maps to the invalid_arguments reason; no AC asserts reason values. Map to none or register a distinct reason with an oracle.
A3: "the completing path AC43 asserts unconditionally" re-reads as reinstating the removed unconditional claim; write "the completing path, which AC43 asserts unconditionally".
A4: parenthetical forbids literal shift values while listing them; delete the parenthetical.
F1: C1 container half still unfalsifiable — a zero-charged namespace container passes AC7; assert the retained namespace set structurally (as AC38 does) after churn.
F2: retirement ranges stop at 802-812/950-962 but the cleanup calls are at 813/966; widen ranges or name the seam calls by symbol.
